perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s perspective, he has access to:

- Keith and Elizabeth are colleagues at the construction company: Keith is a construction worker and Elizabeth is the receptionist. They normally have a friendly but professional relationship, often interacting when Keith visits the office for paperwork and project updates.
- Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him over the past few days.
- Keith wondered whether he had upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her.
- Keith heard Elizabeth say no, she was not upset; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her.
- Keith told Elizabeth he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break.
- Keith heard Elizabeth accept, say it was kind, and thank him.
- Over the coffee break, Keith heard Elizabeth share more about her stresses; he perceived them as quite severe.
- Keith suggested Elizabeth consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help.
- Keith heard Elizabeth say she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn after his suggestion.
- Keith believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her or overstepped, and he felt regretful.
- Keith told Elizabeth he hoped he had not overstepped, and that he wanted her to know he was there to support her no matter what.
- Keith heard Elizabeth say he did not overstep, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative toward him.
- Keith believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- Keith told Elizabeth he was glad they talked and that he is always there if she needs to chat or take a break.
- Keith heard Elizabeth thank him, say it meant a lot, and say she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship.

Keith does not have access to Elizabeth’s unspoken thoughts, private reasons, or any events he did not observe or hear directly.
